Incineroar leads to use Intimidate and Fake Out against the physical attackers. Gholdengo's Thunderbolt punishes the Water types Palafin and Toxapex, and Garchomp adds fast physical pressure with Earthquake and Stone Edge.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick three from our team against their Palafin, Toxapex, Incineroar, Annihilape, Chandelure, and Tinkaton. Incineroar seems like a solid lead with intimidate, fake out, and parting shot, and I'm weighing Kingambit's matchup since its Dark-type moves hit neutrally against their Steel/Fairy Tinkaton.

Garchomp looks safe against Chandelure and can threaten Toxapex with Earthquake, while Gholdengo's Thunderbolt could be strong against Water-type Palafin and Toxapex. I'm leaning toward Incineroar, Garchomp, and Gholdengo as a balanced trio for coverage, though Kingambit's Sword Dance set against Annihilape is tempting too.

decisions.thought: 76% MOVE: closecombat, 22% MOVE: earthquake, 2% SWITCH: tinkaton

Fake Out does nothing because Annihilape is Ghost-type and immune to Normal moves. Annihilape is faster, so Flare Blitz will not be preempted, and it hits Annihilape for neutral damage. Parting Shot risks triggering Defiant.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm noting Fake Out is legal but has no effect on Annihilape, likely because it has Inner Focus blocking flinch, though it still lands as a damaging priority move.

Now I'm weighing switch options like Protect to scout or Parting Shot to pivot into Gholdengo or Garchomp, checking how their typing interacts with Annihilape's Fighting-type attacks like Close Combat.

Fighting is super effective against Dark, so Close Combat would hit Incineroar hard, but Defiant only triggers on actual stat drops, not just being at -1. I think Protect is the safest call here to scout Annihilape's move without risking a boost.

decisions.thought: 55% SWITCH: chandelure, 45% SWITCH: tinkaton
40% MOVE: fireblast [MEGA], 15% MOVE: shadowball [MEGA], 13% MOVE: calmmind [MEGA]

Incineroar is at 35 HP and slower than Chandelure, so it could be KO'd before acting, and Flare Blitz is resisted with a recoil risk. Garchomp switches in safely: Fire moves are resisted by its Dragon typing, and it has Earthquake for a 2x hit on Chandelure.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar at only 35 HP, Chandelure being faster and resisting Fire-type moves makes Flare Blitz risky—even if it lands, the recoil from such a weak hit probably wouldn't matter much, but Chandelure's Shadow Ball or Fire Blast could easily finish off Incineroar first.

Switching looks safer: Gholdengo is vulnerable since Steel is doubly weak to Chandelure's Fire-type attacks, but Garchomp seems promising since Earthquake hits Chandelure for super effective damage as a Fire/Ghost type, and Garchomp's healthy HP pool gives it room to operate.

Parting Shot with Incineroar is risky since Chandelure's speed lets it strike first, possibly KOing the already weakened Incineroar before the stat drop lands. Switching straight to Garchomp seems like the safer play.

Garchomp is faster than Chandelure, and Earthquake is super effective against its Fire typing. Mega Garchomp boosts Attack a lot, so Earthquake should knock Chandelure out before it moves. Fire Blast is only neutral against Mega Garchomp, so Garchomp is safe this turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking matchup math: Mega Chandelure's Fire Blast isn't very effective against Garchomp's Dragon typing, and Mega Garchomp's speed likely outpaces Chandelure anyway, so this isn't a favorable attack line.

Meanwhile Garchomp's Earthquake is super effective against Chandelure's Fire side, and with Mega Garchomp's boosted Attack this hits hard enough to potentially nearly knock Chandelure out in one shot despite its decent bulk.

Also Fire against Mega Garchomp's typing works out neutral since the Dragon resistance and Ground weakness cancel out.

decisions.thought: 71% MOVE: swordsdance, 26% MOVE: knockoff, 3% MOVE: stealthrock

Gholdengo's Steel/Ghost typing makes Tinkaton's hits neutral, and Gigaton Hammer threatens a big hit back. Nasty Plot would leave Gholdengo exposed to another Gigaton Hammer. Shadow Ball gets STAB damage now and may drop Tinkaton's Sp. Def.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm thinking about the opponent's Mega Tinkaton, Fairy/Steel typing, against Gholdengo's Steel/Ghost typing, weighing Steel's weaknesses to Fire, Ground, and Fighting along with its resistance to Fairy attacks.

Tinkaton's Gigaton Hammer just hit hard, and with its physical power it could deal major damage to Gholdengo's lower defense—likely 60-70% per hit, meaning Gholdengo can't tank two in a row. Setting up Nasty Plot is tempting since Good as Gold blocks status, but I need to weigh whether Gholdengo survives long enough to capitalize.

Checking attack options: Shadow Ball with Life Orb and STAB looks like the strongest reliable hit against Tinkaton's special bulk, outperforming Thunderbolt which lacks STAB, while Makeitrain's self-inflicted SpA drop makes it risky despite higher base power.

Given speed uncertainty, I think dealing consistent damage now matters more than setting up Nasty Plot and hoping to survive a counterattack. Shadow Ball is the pragmatic choice—solid damage plus a chance at a defensive debuff.

decisions.thought: 84% MOVE: knockoff, 12% MOVE: swordsdance, 3% MOVE: gigatonhammer

Tinkaton is at 31% and Shadow Ball is a STAB Ghost attack that is neutral into Fairy/Steel. Gholdengo's 203 Sp. Atk with Life Orb should easily KO it. Gholdengo is faster or close to it, so this should finish the threat before Gigaton Hammer lands.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking type matchups for Tinkaton against Gholdengo's Shadow Ball - since Tinkaton is Fairy/Steel, Ghost doesn't get any special advantage against it, so this attack would only deal neutral damage.

Thunderbolt and Make It Rain also hit Tinkaton for neutral damage since Electric isn't resisted by Steel and the Steel/Fairy typing against those moves evens out. Gholdengo's SpA is 203 with Life Orb boosting Shadow Ball's 80 base power, while Tinkaton's SpD sits in the 112-172 range at 31% remaining HP.

Shadow Ball with STAB and Life Orb should deal huge damage against Tinkaton's defenses and likely secures the KO, while Thunderbolt lacks STAB and offers no real advantage here. There's some risk if Tinkaton outspeeds and lands a boosted Gigaton Hammer, but Shadow Ball remains the clear best option given its reliable accuracy and power.

83% MOVE: gigatonhammer, 10% MOVE: knockoff, 4% MOVE: swordsdance

Tinkaton outspeeds Incineroar, and Incineroar's 35 HP leaves it dead to any +2 Gigaton Hammer before Flare Blitz can act. Protect only delays a turn. Parting Shot drops Tinkaton's Attack and brings in my last Pokémon without taking a hit.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar is at 35 HP and Tinkaton is mega with 31% HP and +2 attack, so Fake Out won't work since it's not the first turn. Flare Blitz would be super effective against Tinkaton's steel typing, but Tinkaton is faster and its Gigaton Hammer could knock out Incineroar first, so I'm weighing whether Incineroar's fire attack can get through before that happens.

Protect could buy a turn since priority beats Tinkaton's move, blocking damage entirely, though Tinkaton's speed advantage still limits what comes after. Parting Shot would let me switch out while weakening Tinkaton's attack, which might be safer than risking Flare Blitz not landing.

Parting shot would bring in whichever teammate remains after Gholdengo fainted, weakening Tinkaton's attack by a stage in the process, though that costs tempo if I'm not sure that last mon can actually threaten Tinkaton.

I'll go with Parting Shot—it gets value by cutting Tinkaton's attack to soften a future Gigaton, plus brings in the last mon safely, even though that mon's strength is unknown.
